headline: Anne Arundel County's council in Maryland has voted unanimously to pause new data center projects while a work group studies rules for them.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a unanimous county vote with a defined end date; local scale.
importance_line: Residents, developers and landowners in Anne Arundel County face a pause on new data centers while rules are drafted, but the rules themselves are not yet written and the reports differ on the exact length.
summary: The Capital Gazette reports that the Anne Arundel County Council in Maryland voted unanimously on Monday 5 Oct 2026 to approve a moratorium (a pause) on data center projects in the county, which the paper's headline calls a 15-month pause. WBAL News Radio reported before the vote that the pause would last until 31 Jan 2028 or until the county adopts rules, while a work group studies energy and water use, noise, air quality and other effects and recommends regulations.
notes: The Capital Gazette article body did not load; the facts come from its summary line and from WBAL's report of the same day, written before the vote. The Gazette's headline says 15 months while its summary line says 18; WBAL gave an end date of 31 Jan 2028 for the version before the vote. The Baltimore Sun carries the same article by Benjamin Rothstein.
